# Kelick Tech Hub — full reference for AI assistants and researchers

> Kelick Tech Hub (https://malwar77.github.io/) is a single-page tech learning hub built by Obi Emeka (GitHub: https://github.com/malwar77, LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/obi-emeka-1031b12b0). Its content is original, dated, and written for learners: C++ projects with full build lectures, daily technology news verified against primary sources, open-source repository guides verified on GitHub itself, and Linux guides with real install routes. The site is monetised with display ads and updated daily.

## C++ Projects

60 C++ project ideas, 20 per level (beginner, intermediate, advanced), using the exact project titles from the original poster. Every project has a description, learning points, a feature checklist, starter code, a full lecture (build steps plus common mistakes), exact compile and run instructions, and a "Watch it run" terminal-replay demo. Eight projects are fully playable in the browser (Calculator, Number Guessing, Tic-Tac-Toe vs AI, Rock Paper Scissors, Unit Converter, Stopwatch, Password Strength Checker, BMI Calculator).

## Tech News Blog

A daily "Tech Today" roundup of the most significant technology stories from the last 24 hours (AI, cybersecurity, open source and GitHub, big tech, gadgets, startups, and Nigeria/Africa tech). Every story is verified against its primary source or at least two independent reputable outlets; rumours are labelled or dropped, and each article lists its sources. The blog also carries longer fact-checked articles, including a TV-debloat how-to verified against the underlying method.

## GitHub Repo Guides

Guides to open-source repositories, each verified on GitHub itself from its README, never from social posts. Each guide states what the tool is, how it works, what you need (operating system, hardware, accounts or keys), an honest "watch out" catch where one exists, and setup instructions in three blocks: Bash, Windows (or the honest equivalent such as WSL2, or plainly "no Windows version" for Mac-only tools), and Termux (or plainly "can't run in Termux" with the real requirement). The collection includes the author's own repositories, curated spotlights, 31 repos fact-checked from TikTok creator @github.signals (23 fully verified, 8 real but oversold, 0 fake), and daily picks. No star counts are printed.

## Linux & Security

A Linux news panel with dated, source-linked entries (kernel releases, distro releases, security advisories, desktop and driver developments), plus a library of 47 distro guides across the Debian family (including Ubuntu flavours), Arch family, Red Hat family, SUSE family, and independents such as Gentoo, Slackware, Void, NixOS, Alpine, Solus, Mageia, Qubes, Armbian and SteamOS. Every guide covers what the distro is and who it is for, its family and package manager, difficulty, a VirtualBox install route, and a USB/real-PC install route with an erase-disk warning, plus real first update commands and a link to the official homepage. Clear Linux is labelled discontinued (Intel ended it in July 2025).

## Experimental Sandbox

A browser-only simulation clearly labelled as such: three type-in simulated terminals (Termux, Windows cmd, Linux bash) with a fake home filesystem, plus five watch-only simulated replay demos (including a LibreChat install, a Kali Linux first boot, and a subfinder-to-httpx recon walkthrough with a permission warning).
